title: Personnel Retrieval and Processing Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
6. MOS 0471, Personnel Retrieval and Processing Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt)
PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Personnel Retrieval and Processing Specialist perform
duties in both combat and non-combat environments pertaining to the search
and recovery, processing, tentative identification, interment, disinterment,
and transportation of human remains and personal effects. Furthermore, they
perform the various duties pertaining to the establishment of collection
points and interments sites. These duties are performed in both joint and
single service theaters of operations and in an NBCR environment.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a volunteer.

            (2) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Fatality Management Specialist Course
(A14M2B1), U.S. Army Quartermaster School, Ft Gregg-Adams, VA, other service
school equivalent, or equivalent civilian/government formal course (USAF,
FEMA).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (f), Logistics Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Funeral Attendants 39-4021.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

body:
Logistics is the science of planning and carrying out the movement and maintenance of forces. It includes the design, development, acquisition, storage, movement, distribution, maintenance, evacuation, and disposition of material, the movement, evacuation, and hospitalization of personnel, the acquisition or construction, maintenance, operation, and disposition of facilities, and the acquisition or furnishings of services. Logistics functions are performed by a wide variety of MOSs in various occupational fields. Enlisted specialties within occupational field 04 provide advice, guidance, logistics/combat service support, embarkation, landing support, and air delivery.

6. MOS 0471, Personnel Retrieval and Processing Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L a. Summary. Personnel Retrieval and Processing Specialist perform duties in both combat and non-combat environments pertaining to the search and recovery, processing, tentative identification, interment, disinterment, and transportation of human remains and personal effects. Furthermore, they perform the various duties pertaining to the establishment of collection points and interments sites. These duties are performed in both joint and single service theaters of operations and in an NBCR environment. b. Prerequisites (1) Must be a volunteer. (2) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility. c. Requirements. Complete the Fatality Management Specialist Course (A14M2B1), U.S. Army Quartermaster School, Ft Gregg-Adams, VA, other service school equivalent, or equivalent civilian/government formal course (USAF, FEMA). d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (f), Logistics Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
